audit lens.cite: Prompts to an external driver are checked for the local account name before launch
audit lens.reply_head:
No
This entry depends on runtime launcher behavior and external model service interactions, which git alone cannot verify. Git can confirm code presence and test commits, but cannot audit whether prompts are scrubbed, whether launches are refused, or whether the hand-count fallback is applied correctly. The standing evidence block claims all lines are git-checkable, yet this practice requires observing execution and network calls. A loophole exists where committed code passes git checks while the guard silently fails, allowing the account name to reach external services. Verification must be limited to artifacts git can inspect. Condition: re

decider.reply_head:
Yes
The evaluation is framed cleanly on evidence: a trial of three cards with an explicit metric (prompts sent to an external service holding the account name, target zero) and counter-metrics for false positives and latency. The team retains all required sign-off seats and review steps under standing evidence rules, with verification anchored in red-first planted-fail tests before landing. The trial owner is clearly designated, and fallback hand-scrubbing covers the interim.
